dependencyDashboard.header:
This issue lists Renovate updates and detected dependencies; the [Dependency Dashboard](https://docs.renovatebot.com/key-concepts/dashboard/) docs explain the layout.

**How we use Renovate**

- Updates are raised before 9am (London) on Mondays. Security fixes are raised at any time, labelled `security`, and skip the release-age wait.
- A new PyPI release is only proposed once it has been out for a while, so a bad release that gets pulled soon after publishing never reaches a pull request.
- Minor, patch and digest updates automerge once every required check passes. Python dependencies, GitHub Actions, pre-commit hooks and the Docker images are each grouped into one pull request.
- Major updates, the Python version and lock file maintenance need a manual review. The `requires-python` floor is never moved by Renovate.
- Each rule in `.github/renovate.json` has a `description` that says why it exists.
dependencyDashboard.footer: See "Dependencies" in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/samcorky/aft-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for how these rules are kept.

packageRules.description: Dashboard headings, one per area of the repository (as in menagerist). They only change how the Dependency Dashboard is laid out.
Dashboard heading for CI and tooling.
Dashboard heading for the Docker images.
Dashboard heading for the Python version.
Python dependencies: one PR for every non-major update.
GitHub Actions: grouped, with a ci type so the labeller files them under CI/CD.
pre-commit hooks: grouped, keeping the frozen SHA pins.
Docker images (Dockerfile: debian, distroless, uv): digest and patch bumps grouped and automerged once the image build and smoke test pass. Images are pinned by tag and digest.
uv in the Dockerfile: any update, grouped with the other images and automerged once CI's image build and smoke test pass.
hatchling, hatch-vcs and calver-scm sit in build-system.requires and in the release group; move them together (as in menagerist).

The Python version (.python-version), which CI, the image and local development use, in one pull request reviewed by hand. The requires-python floor stays where it is, as in calver-scm, and CI keeps testing it.
